q.s: Kalibangan, the Harappan site on the Ghaggar in Rajasthan, was excavated during 1961–69 by:
q.x: B.B. Lal and B.K. Thapar dug Kalibangan in 1961–69; R.S. Bisht excavated Dholavira and S.R. Rao Lothal.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Kalibangan is correct?
o: Kalibangan was excavated by R.S. Bisht.
Kalibangan lies on the bank of the Ravi.
q.x: Kalibangan-I (pre-Harappan) was fortified in mud brick; the site lies on the Ghaggar and was dug by B.B. Lal and B.K. Thapar.

q.s: Harappa, the first Indus site to be excavated, is located on the bank of the river:
q.x: Harappa (Montgomery district, Punjab, Pakistan) lies on the Ravi; Mohenjodaro is on the Indus.

q.s: Which Harappan site is NOT correctly matched with its river?
q.x: Rangpur in Gujarat lies on the Bhadar.

q.s: Which Harappan site has yielded evidence of lipstick and a bead and toy making workshop?
q.x: Chanhudaro, the only Harappan city without a citadel, was a craft centre where lipstick and a toy/bead factory were found.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT known to the Harappans?
q.x: The Harappans used copper and bronze but not iron; dice, bronze mirrors and ivory combs have been found.

q.s: The famous 'Pashupati' seal of the Indus Valley Civilisation was found at:
q.x: The steatite Pashupati seal, with a three-faced horned figure in yogic posture, was found at Mohenjodaro.

q.s: Which of the following animals is NOT shown around the seated figure on the Pashupati seal?
q.x: The figure is surrounded by an elephant, tiger, rhinoceros and buffalo, with two deer below the seat; no bull is shown.

q.s: The Pali text Milindapanho is a dialogue between the monk Nagasena and which Indo-Greek king?
q.x: Milinda of the Milindapanho is the Indo-Greek king Menander, who questions the monk Nagasena.

q.s: The Rigvedic river Kubha is identified with the modern river:
q.x: Kubha – Kabul, Krumu – Kurram, Gomati – Gomal, Suvastu – Swat: rivers showing the Aryans' link with Afghanistan.

q.s: Which of the following Rigvedic rivers is NOT correctly matched with its modern name?
q.x: Suvastu is the Swat; the other three pairs are correct.

q.s: The Battle of Ten Kings, described in the Rigveda, was won by which Bharata king?
q.x: Sudas of the Bharata (Tritsu) family defeated a confederacy of ten kings on the Parushni (Ravi), described in Mandala VII.

q.s: The priest who supported King Sudas in the Battle of Ten Kings was:
q.x: Vasishtha was Sudas' priest; Vishvamitra sided with the confederacy of ten kings.

q.s: In the Rigveda, the tribal chief (Rajan) was often called 'Gopati', which means:
q.x: Cattle were the chief wealth, so the Rajan was the Gopati; he ruled people, not a fixed territory.

q.s: The chief queen of the early Vedic Rajan was known as:
q.x: The chief queen was the Mahisi; Parivrikti was the discarded wife.

q.s: Which of the following Rigvedic officials is NOT correctly matched with his role?
q.x: The Madhyamasi was a mediator; the Spasa was the spy.

q.s: In Later Vedic society, which varna was the only tribute-paying section?
q.x: The Vaishyas (farmers, herders, traders, artisans) alone paid tribute (bali); Brahmanas and Kshatriyas were exempt.

q.s: Pratityasamutpada, the doctrine of dependent origination, belongs to:
q.x: Pratityasamutpada is a Buddhist doctrine: every phenomenon arises from a cause.

q.s: How many links (nidanas) are there in the Buddhist chain of dependent origination?
q.x: The chain has twelve nidanas, from Avidya (ignorance) to Jara-marana (old age and death).

q.s: The earliest Jain scriptures, which are now lost, are known as the fourteen:
q.x: The 14 Purvas were held in the 12th Anga (Drishtivada), which is now lost.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a group of the Ang-bahya texts of the Jain canon?
q.x: The Ang-bahya texts are 12 Upangas, 10 Prakirnas, 6 Chhedasutras and 4 Mulasutras; the Purvas belonged to the Anga Drishtivada.

q.s: The Kadalalaya Basadi (1117 CE) was built by Mailama, wife of a minister of which dynasty?
q.x: Mailama was the wife of the Kakatiya minister Betana; the Nedumba Vasati at Bejawada was built by the Eastern Chalukya queen Ayyana Mahadevi.

q.s: Which of the following Jain shrines is NOT correctly matched with its builder?
o: Pan Supari Bazar Jinalaya – Devaraya II
q.x: The Kadalalaya Basadi was built by Mailama, wife of the Kakatiya minister Betana.

q.s: The Sanskrit drama Mudrarakshasa, on Chanakya's victory over the Nanda minister Rakshasa, was written by:
q.x: Vishakhadatta wrote the Mudrarakshasa in the Gupta age; it is a source on Chandragupta Maurya's rise.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Mudrarakshasa is correct?
o: It is a Prakrit drama of the Mauryan age.
In it Chanakya wins over Rakshasa, the minister of the Nandas.
It was written by Kautilya himself.
q.x: Vishakhadatta's Sanskrit play of the Gupta age tells how Chanakya won over Rakshasa for Chandragupta Maurya.

q.s: The main currency of the Mauryan period consisted of:
q.x: The Mauryas issued no gold coins; their currency was the punch-marked silver coin.

q.s: Kautilya's saying 'a chariot cannot move on one wheel' stresses the king's need for:
q.x: The saying justifies the Mantriparishad: the king cannot rule without ministers.

q.s: The chief source for the kings of Vengi, Avamukta and Devarashtra defeated by Samudragupta is the:
q.x: Harisena's Allahabad Pillar prashasti lists the twelve southern kings Samudragupta defeated.

q.s: Avamukta, one of the southern kingdoms conquered by Samudragupta, was ruled by:
q.x: Nilaraja ruled Avamukta; Ugrasena ruled Palakka, Hastivarman Vengi and Kubera Devarashtra.

q.s: Ghantasala, a Buddhist centre and port of the early historical period, is in which district of Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: Ghantasala (Kontakossylla of the classical writers) is in Krishna district.

q.s: Which port of the Gupta age is NOT correctly matched with its location?
q.x: Chaul lay on the Konkan coast south of Mumbai.

q.s: The Kalika Purana, an Upapurana probably composed in Assam, is associated with:
q.x: The Kalika Purana is a Shakta Upapurana, not one of the 18 Mahapuranas.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Kalika Purana is correct?
o: It is one of the 18 Mahapuranas.
q.x: The Kalika Purana is a Shakta Upapurana, probably written in Assam.

q.s: The Sanskrit play Mrichchhakatika was written by:
q.x: Shudraka wrote the Mrichchhakatika ('The Little Clay Cart').

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: Thirteen plays are attributed to Shudraka.
The Devichandraguptam deals with Ramagupta and Dhruvadevi.
The Mrichchhakatika was written by Bhasa.
The Mudrarakshasa was written by Kalidasa.
q.x: The Devichandraguptam deals with Ramagupta and Dhruvadevi; thirteen plays are attributed to Bhasa, the Mrichchhakatika is Shudraka's and the Mudrarakshasa Vishakhadatta's.

q.s: In Chola village administration, the committee that looked after tanks and the distribution of water was the:
q.x: The eri variyam managed tanks; the totta variyam gardens and the pon variyam gold.

q.s: Land whose revenue was set apart for the repair of village tanks in Chola times was called:
q.x: Eripatti land paid for tank repair; brahmadeya was land granted to Brahmanas and devadana to temples.

q.s: Balban, who later broke the power of the 'Forty' (Chahalgani), had been bought as a slave by:
q.x: Iltutmish bought Balban, who rose to be one of the Forty and later naib to Nasiruddin Mahmud.

q.s: Which Delhi Sultan created the military department Diwan-i-Arz, separating it from the Diwan-i-Wizarat?
q.x: Balban set up the Diwan-i-Arz under the Ariz-i-Mamalik to reorganise the army.

q.s: The system of 'dagh' introduced by Alauddin Khalji refers to:
q.x: Dagh was the branding of horses; huliya (chehra) was the descriptive roll of soldiers.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a military measure of Alauddin Khalji?
q.x: Alauddin paid his standing army in cash, not through iqtas.

q.s: Sikandar Lodi extended his rule from Punjab to Bihar and subdued the ruler of:
q.x: Sikandar Lodi subdued Jaunpur and defeated Bengal rulers and Rajput chiefs.

q.s: The city of Agra was founded in 1504 by:
q.x: Sikandar Lodi founded Agra and made it his capital.

q.s: The only woman ruler of the Delhi Sultanate was:
q.x: Razia ruled Delhi from 1236 to 1240; Rudrama Devi was a Kakatiya ruler.

q.s: Which woman is NOT correctly matched with her identity?
o: Razia – Only woman ruler of Delhi
q.x: Lal Ded was a woman saint of Kashmir.

q.s: Chandayan (1379), an early Awadhi premakhyan (Sufi romance), was written by:
q.x: Mulla Daud wrote Chandayan; Qutban wrote Mrigavati and Jayasi the Padmavat.

q.s: The Sufi romance Padmavat was written by:
q.x: Malik Muhammad Jayasi wrote Padmavat in Awadhi in the 16th century.

q.s: The Razmnama, produced at Akbar's court, is the Persian translation of the:
q.x: The Razmnama is the Persian Mahabharata made under Akbar.

q.s: Which of the following Persian works is NOT correctly matched with its source?
o: Dalail-i-Firoz Shahi – Sanskrit texts of the Jwalamukhi temple
q.x: The Tutinama of Nakhshabi is based on the Suka Saptati.

q.s: At the Battle of Chausa (1539), Sher Shah defeated:
q.x: Sher Shah beat Humayun at Chausa (1539) and again at Kannauj (1540).

q.s: Which of the following battles was NOT fought by Babur?
q.x: Babur fought Panipat (1526), Khanwa (1527), Chanderi (1528) and Ghaghra (1529); Chausa (1539) was Humayun's defeat by Sher Shah.

q.s: Aurangzeb re-imposed the jizya in the year:
q.x: Akbar abolished the jizya in 1564; Aurangzeb re-imposed it in 1679.

q.s: Officers appointed by Aurangzeb to see that people lived according to the Sharia were called:
q.x: Muhtasibs were censors of public morals; zawabit were state-made secular regulations.

q.s: The philosophy of Shuddhadvaita and the Pushtimarga ('path of grace') are associated with:
q.x: Vallabha taught Shuddhadvaita; Nimbarka taught Dvaitadvaita and Madhva Dvaita.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: Nimbarka taught that God, souls and the world are eternally distinct.
Chaitanya's philosophy is known as Shuddhadvaita.
Ramanuja taught salvation through devotion and prapatti (self-surrender) to Vishnu.
q.x: Ramanuja taught bhakti and prapatti; eternal distinction is Madhva's Dvaita, Chaitanya taught Achintya Bhedabheda and the Pushtimarga accepted householder life.

q.s: Peshwa Madhav Rao I, after whose death Peshwa control over the Maratha chiefs weakened, died in:
q.x: Madhav Rao I died in 1772; Panipat was fought in 1761.

q.s: The Third Battle of Panipat was fought in:
q.x: Ahmad Shah Abdali defeated the Marathas at Panipat in 1761; Plassey was 1757, Wandiwash 1760 and Buxar 1764.

q.s: Brazil's famous Nelore breed of cattle traces its origin to which district of Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: Nelore cattle descend from cattle taken from the Nellore region of Andhra Pradesh.

q.s: The Portuguese navigator who reached Brazil in 1500 and set up the first Portuguese factory at Calicut was:
q.x: Cabral reached Brazil and then Calicut in 1500; Vasco da Gama had reached Calicut in 1498.

q.s: The attack on the British Residency at Hyderabad on 17 July 1857 was led by:
q.x: Turrebaz Khan and Maulvi Allauddin led the attack from the Mecca Masjid.

q.s: Korukonda Subba Reddy led the rising of 1857–58 in which region?
q.x: Subba Reddy led the rising at Errannagudem in the Godavari Agency.

q.s: Siraj-ud-Daula suspected the English of supporting which of his rivals at court?
q.x: The English were seen to back Ghaseti Begum and Shaukat Jang of Purnea; Mir Madan and Mohan Lal fought loyally for Siraj at Plassey.

q.s: The First Anglo-Maratha War ended with the Treaty of:
q.x: The Treaty of Salbai (May 1782) with Mahadji Sindhia ended the First war; Bassein (1802) led to the Second.

q.s: The Peshwaship was abolished (1818) after the Third Anglo-Maratha War during the rule of:
q.x: Under Lord Hastings the Third war ended the Peshwaship in June 1818.

q.s: Majnum Shah and Bhawani Pathak were leaders of the:
q.x: The Sanyasi revolt (1763–1800) in Bengal was led by Majnum Shah and Bhawani Pathak and subdued by Warren Hastings.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT associated with the Sanyasi Revolt?
q.x: Titu Mir led the Wahabi-inspired Barasat rising; the others were linked with the Sanyasi revolt.

q.s: By the Treaty of Hyderabad (1766), the English obtained the Northern Circars from:
q.x: Nizam Ali leased the Circars by the 1766 treaty for Rs 9 lakh a year or military aid.

q.s: The Mughal emperor who granted the Northern Circars to the English by a farman in 1765 was:
q.x: Clive obtained the farman from Shah Alam II; Nizam Ali at first refused to accept it.

q.s: The system of Subsidiary Alliance was perfected and widely applied by:
q.x: Dupleix first hired out troops to Indian rulers; Wellesley turned it into the Subsidiary Alliance.

q.s: The Nizam gave the 'Ceded Districts' (Rayalaseema) to the British in 1800 in lieu of:
o: Debts to the Nawab of Carnatic
q.x: When the Nizam could not pay for the subsidiary force he ceded the districts won from Mysore.

q.s: Raja Ram Mohan Roy founded the Vedanta College in the year:
q.x: Ram Mohan Roy founded the Vedanta College in 1825.

q.s: Mayo College at Ajmer (1875) was set up to educate:
q.x: Mayo College was founded for the sons of the ruling princely families.

q.s: The Communist Party of India held its founding conference at Kanpur in:
q.x: The CPI conference at Kanpur was held in December 1925, after the Kanpur Bolshevik conspiracy case of 1924.

q.s: Philip Spratt and Ben Bradley were among the accused in the:
q.x: The Meerut case (1929) tried communist and trade-union leaders, including Britons Spratt, Bradley and Hutchinson.

q.s: The Rowlatt Act was passed in:
q.x: The Rowlatt Act was passed in March 1919 to replace the wartime Defence of India Act with a permanent law.

q.s: The Rowlatt Act was based on the report of the:
q.x: The Sedition Committee headed by Justice Sidney Rowlatt recommended it; the Hunter Committee probed Jallianwala Bagh.

q.s: The Non-Brahmin Manifesto of December 1916, which led to the Justice Party, was issued by:
q.x: Thyagaraya Chetty signed the Non-Brahmin Manifesto; the South Indian People's Association was formed in November 1916.

q.s: The symbol of the Justice Party was the:
q.x: The Justice Party's emblem was the scales; the party took its name from its English daily 'Justice'.

q.s: Ambedkar's satyagraha for drawing water from the Chavdar Tank (March 1927) took place at:
q.x: The Mahad Satyagraha was held at the Chavdar Tank on 20 March 1927; the Manusmriti was burnt there on 25 December 1927.

q.s: The Kalaram Temple Entry Satyagraha (1930–35) led by Ambedkar was held at:
q.x: The Kalaram Temple Satyagraha took place at Nashik from March 1930 to 1935.

q.s: Which of the following movements was anti-British and welcomed the Indian National Congress?
q.x: The Deoband school was anti-British and welcomed the Congress, while the Aligarh Movement was loyal to the British and opposed the Congress.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: The Deoband Movement was loyal to the British.
The Aligarh Movement opposed the Indian National Congress.
The Deoband Movement opposed the Congress.
q.x: Aligarh was loyal to the British and opposed the Congress; Deoband was anti-British and welcomed the Congress.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched with its year of founding?
q.x: The Ahmadiya Movement dates from 1889; 1866 is the year of the Deoband school.

q.s: The Ahmadiya Movement (1889) was founded by:
q.x: Mirza Ghulam Ahmad founded it at Qadian; Shariatullah led the Faraizis and Nanotvi founded Deoband.

q.s: Which reform body is NOT correctly matched with the community it worked among?
q.x: The Singh Sabha worked among the Sikhs.

q.s: The bomb attack on Viceroy Lord Hardinge in Chandni Chowk, Delhi (December 1912), was organised by:
q.x: Rash Behari Bose planned the attack and later escaped to Japan; Hardinge was only wounded.

q.s: The bomb at Lord Hardinge in the Delhi Conspiracy (1912) was thrown by:
q.x: Basanta Kumar Biswas threw the bomb on 23 December 1912.

q.s: The Provisional Government of Azad Hind was proclaimed by Subhas Chandra Bose on 21 October 1943 at:
q.x: It was proclaimed at Singapore; its headquarters later moved to Rangoon.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Azad Hind Government is correct?
o: It was recognised by no country other than Japan.
It renamed the Andaman Islands as Netaji Dweep.
It declared war on Britain and the USA.
q.x: It declared war on Britain and the USA, was recognised by nine countries, and renamed the Andaman and Nicobar Islands Shaheed Dweep and Swaraj Dweep.

q.s: The repression of the Civil Disobedience Movement during 1932–34 was carried out under Viceroy:
q.x: Lord Willingdon crushed the second phase of Civil Disobedience; Irwin was Viceroy during the Dandi March and the 1931 Pact.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: The police firing at Berhampore took place on 15 January 1932.
Lord Irwin was Viceroy during the repression of 1932–34.
The Gandhi–Irwin Pact was signed in 1932.
Lord Willingdon was Viceroy during the Dandi March.
q.x: Berhampore firing was in January 1932 under Willingdon; Irwin was Viceroy during the Dandi March and the 1931 Pact.

q.s: After its ban was lifted in July 1942, the Communist Party of India's stand on the Quit India Movement was to:
o: Oppose it and support the war effort
Support it only in the princely states
q.x: Calling it a 'People's War', the CPI backed the British war effort and opposed Quit India.

q.s: The first open Communist conference in Andhra was held in 1943 at:
q.x: The Third Communist Conference at Vijayawada (1943), with Chandra Rajeswara Rao as secretary, was the first open one in Andhra.

q.s: The Sri Bagh Pact of 1937 was an agreement between leaders of coastal Andhra and:
q.x: The pact, signed at Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao's house 'Sri Bagh' in Madras, met Rayalaseema's concerns.

q.s: Under the Sri Bagh Pact, the two centres of Andhra University were to be at Waltair and:
q.x: The pact gave Andhra University centres at Waltair and Anantapur and priority to Rayalaseema and Nellore in river waters for 10 years.

q.s: The Andhra Mahasabha session of 1916, which demanded a separate Andhra Congress circle, was held at:
q.x: The Kakinada session (1916) demanded a separate Andhra circle; the Nellore session (1917) rejected the inclusion of Madras city.

q.s: Which body, founded in 1903, is regarded as the cradle of the Andhra movement?
q.x: The Guntur Youngmen's Literary Association (1903) began the Andhra movement; the Andhra Jana Sangham came in 1921.

q.s: The States Reorganisation Commission announced by Nehru in December 1953 was headed by:
q.x: Justice Fazl Ali headed it, with K.M. Panikkar and H.N. Kunzru as members; S.K. Dhar headed the 1948 Linguistic Provinces Commission.

q.s: Andhra State, whose creation set off demands for linguistic states elsewhere, came into being on:
q.x: Andhra State was formed on 1 October 1953; Potti Sriramulu had died on 15 December 1952.

q.s: The Gentlemen's Agreement of 1956 was signed on behalf of Andhra State by its Chief Minister:
q.x: Bezawada Gopala Reddy signed as CM of Andhra State; Burgula Ramakrishna Rao signed as CM of Hyderabad.

q.s: K.V. Ranga Reddy signed the Gentlemen's Agreement of 1956 as:
q.x: K.V. Ranga Reddy was Deputy CM of Hyderabad; J.V. Narsing Rao signed as Hyderabad PCC President.

q.s: In the Hyderabad State elections of 1952, the People's Democratic Front was the electoral front of the:
q.x: The PDF was the Communists' front in Hyderabad State in 1952.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Visalandhra debate is correct?
o: The People's Democratic Front was the Congress front in 1952.
The Mahila Sabha supported Visalandhra at Hyderabad in May 1954.
The Praja Socialist Party under Mahadeva Singh supported Visalandhra.
q.x: The Mahila Sabha and Hindu Mahasabha backed Visalandhra; the PSP under Mahadeva Singh opposed it; the PDF was the Communists' front.

q.s: Part IX of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 deals with:
o: Management and development of water resources
q.x: Part IX (Sections 84–91) covers water resources; Part II is reorganisation and Part IV the High Court.

q.s: Section 97 of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 amends which Article of the Constitution?
q.x: Section 97 amends Article 371D; Section 96 amends Article 168 for Telangana's Legislative Council.

q.s: The Karle chaitya, the largest rock-cut chaitya hall of the Satavahana age, is located in:
q.x: Karle is in Maharashtra; it is later than the Bhaja caves and has 12 dance-couple sculptures.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Karle chaitya is correct?
o: It is earlier than the Bhaja caves.
It is located in Andhra Pradesh.
It is later than the Bhaja caves.
q.x: Karle, a Buddhist chaitya in Maharashtra, is later than Bhaja and has 12 dance-couple sculptures.

q.s: The Sarvadevadhivasam temple at Nagarjunakonda, built by the commander Elisiri, was dedicated to:
q.x: Elisiri's Sarvadevadhivasam was for Kumara Swami; the Pushpabhadraswami temple was for Shiva.

q.s: The Buddhist sect of the Aparasailiyas was centred at:
q.x: The Aparasailiyas were at Nagarjunakonda and the Purvasailiyas at Amaravati.

q.s: The Maha Chaitya at Nagarjunakonda was a Dhatugarbha stupa, which means it enshrined:
q.x: A Dhatugarbha stupa enshrines bodily relics (dhatu); the Maha Chaitya held relics of the Buddha.

q.s: The coins of the Vishnukundins were made of:
o: Iron with a thin copper coating
q.x: Vishnukundin coins were of iron coated with copper, bearing the lion and other symbols.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Vishnukundin coins is correct?
o: They were made of pure gold.
They were brought to light by Rayaprolu Subrahmanyam.
The lion is the only symbol on them.
q.x: Sixteen types are known, bearing the lion, Nandi, ship and conch.

q.s: Pingali Surana's Raghavapandaviyam is an early Telugu example of a:
q.x: Raghavapandaviyam tells the Ramayana and Mahabharata at once in double-meaning verse (dvyarthi kavya).

q.s: Which Telugu work is NOT correctly matched with its literary form?
q.x: Ranganatha Ramayanam is a Dwipada work; Sugriva Vijayam of Kandukuri Rudrakavi is the first Yakshagana.

q.s: After the Kakatiya fall (1323), Telangana was freed from the Delhi Sultanate by the:
q.x: The Musunuri Nayakas (Prolaya and Kapaya) drove out the Tughluq officers; in Rayalaseema Vijayanagara followed.

q.s: The Kayastha revolt of 1272 against Rudramadevi was led by:
q.x: Ambadeva led the Kayastha revolt; Rudramadevi died fighting him (Chandupatla inscription, 1289).

q.s: Hyderabad city was founded in 1591 by:
q.x: Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah founded Hyderabad and built the Charminar.

q.s: The last Qutb Shahi ruler of Golconda, removed by Aurangzeb in 1687, was:
q.x: Aurangzeb took Golconda in 1687 and imprisoned Abul Hasan Tana Shah.

q.s: Warangal was finally conquered and the Kakatiya kingdom annexed in 1323 by:
q.x: Ulugh Khan, sent by Ghiyasuddin Tughluq, took Warangal after a second siege.

q.s: Ulugh Khan, the conqueror of Warangal (1323), later ruled Delhi as:
q.x: Ulugh Khan, also called Juna Khan, became Sultan Muhammad bin Tughluq in 1325.

q.s: The Laknavaram and Ghanapuram tanks were built during the reign of the Kakatiya ruler:
q.x: Ganapatideva's reign saw many great tanks; Pakhal was built by his officer Jagadala Mummadi.

q.s: Which tank of the Kakatiya and Reddi periods is NOT correctly matched with its builder?
q.x: Pakhal was built by Mummadi Nayaka (Jagadala Mummadi); Mailamba built Bayyaram.

q.s: The Bahmani capital was shifted from Gulbarga to Bidar by:
q.x: Ahmad Shah I moved the capital to Bidar; Gulbarga, the first capital, was renamed Hasanabad.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT one of the five sultanates that arose from the Bahmani kingdom?
q.x: The five were Bijapur, Ahmadnagar, Golconda, Bidar and Berar; Khandesh was a separate kingdom.

q.s: The Sultan of Kashmir known as 'Butshikan' (idol breaker) was:
q.x: Sikandar (1389–1413) was called Butshikan and imposed jizya; Zain-ul-Abidin was tolerant.

q.s: Jonaraja continued Kalhana's Rajatarangini under the patronage of:
q.x: Zain-ul-Abidin had the Rajatarangini translated into Persian and patronised Jonaraja.

q.s: Which of the following pairs of poet and work is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Panduranga Mahatmyam is Tenali Ramakrishna's; Pingali Surana wrote Raghavapandaviyamu and Kalapurnodayamu.

q.s: The Telugu work Panduranga Mahatmyam was written by:
q.x: Tenali Ramakrishna wrote Panduranga Mahatmyam; Peddana wrote Manucharitra.

q.s: The Kota kings, subordinates of the Kakatiyas, ruled Kammanadu with their seat at:
q.x: The Kota family ruled from Dhanyakatakam (Dharanikota); the Pusapatis were of Vizianagaram and the Vatsavayis of Peddapuram.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: The Kota family of Dharanikota was subordinate to the Kakatiyas.
q.x: The Pusapatis were of Vizianagaram, the Vatsavayis of Peddapuram and the Banas of Rayalaseema.

q.s: The Malkapuram inscription (1261) of Rudramadevi's reign records the setting up of:
q.x: The Malkapuram record speaks of a prasuti griha and hospital at Mandadam.

q.s: Which Kakatiya-era inscription is NOT correctly matched with its record?

q.s: The Ramappa temple at Palampet was built by:

q.s: The Ramappa temple was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in:
q.x: The Kakatiya Rudreshwara (Ramappa) temple of 1213 was inscribed in 2021.

q.s: The Nritta Ratnavali, which the Ramappa madanika sculptures follow, was written by:
q.x: Jayapa, a commander of Ganapatideva, wrote the Nritta Ratnavali; Nataraja Ramakrishna revived Perini from it.

q.s: Seesari Charitra (1875), a Telugu rendering of Shakespeare's Julius Caesar, was written by:

q.s: Rajasekhara Charitram, regarded as the first Telugu novel, was written by:

q.s: The 'Ramadandu' volunteer force of the Chirala-Perala movement was organised by:
q.x: Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya, 'Andhra Ratna', formed the Ramadandu.

q.s: The Rama Mohana Library (1911), a landmark of the Andhra library movement, is located at:

q.x: Oggu Katha is performed by the Golla and Kuruma shepherds.

q.s: The Vesara (hybrid) style of temple architecture was started by the:

q.s: The Nagara style of temple architecture is marked by a:
q.x: Nagara temples of North India have a curvilinear shikhara; the pyramidal vimana, gopurams and prakara mark the Dravida style.

q.s: The long-term objective of the National Population Policy 2000 is a stable population by:
q.x: NPP 2000 aims at population stability by 2045; its immediate objective is meeting the unmet need for contraception.

q.s: The medium-term objective of the National Population Policy 2000 was to bring the TFR to 2.1 by:
q.x: The medium-term goal was replacement-level TFR of 2.1 by 2010.

q.s: The concept of 'glocalisation' is associated with:
q.x: Robertson spoke of glocalisation; Giddens of time-space distanciation and Castells of the network society.

q.s: The world-systems idea of core, semi-periphery and periphery was given by:
q.x: Wallerstein's world-systems theory divides the world economy into core, semi-periphery and periphery.

q.s: The first World Social Forum was held in 2001 at:
q.x: The WSF began at Porto Alegre, Brazil, as a counter to the Davos World Economic Forum.

q.s: India hosted the World Social Forum in 2004 at:
q.x: The 2004 WSF was held in Mumbai.

q.x: The Ayagar (Ayagadu) system paid 12 functionaries with manyam land or a harvest share; Bara Balute is Maharashtrian and Jajmani North Indian.

q.x: Jajmani is the North Indian system.

q.s: 'Homo Hierarchicus', a study of the Indian caste system, was written by:

o: Caste, Class and Power – Andre Beteille
Social Background of Indian Nationalism – G.S. Ghurye
Caste and Race in India – G.S. Ghurye

q.s: The Lahore (Pakistan) Resolution of the Muslim League (March 1940) was moved by:
q.x: Fazlul Huq moved the resolution, adopted on 24 March 1940, under Jinnah's presidency.

q.s: The Poona Pact (1932) between Gandhi and Ambedkar was concluded at:
q.x: The Poona Pact was signed in Yerwada Jail, where Gandhi was fasting against separate electorates for the Depressed Classes.

q.s: The 1948–49 committee of Nehru, Patel and Pattabhi Sitaramayya on linguistic provinces is known as the:
q.x: The JVP Committee (Jawaharlal, Vallabhbhai, Pattabhi) followed the Dhar Commission and advised caution on linguistic states.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a member of the States Reorganisation Commission (1953)?
q.x: The SRC was Fazl Ali (chairman), K.M. Panikkar and H.N. Kunzru; it recommended abolishing the Part A/B/C/D classification.

q.s: The Forest Rights Act, 2006 is administered by the Union Ministry of:
q.x: The Ministry of Tribal Affairs is the nodal ministry for the Forest Rights Act.

q.s: Which subject is NOT correctly matched with the Union Ministry that handles it?
o: Welfare of senior citizens – Social Justice and Empowerment
Poshan Abhiyaan – Women and Child Development

q.s: NITI Aayog, which replaced the Planning Commission in 2015, is a:
q.x: NITI Aayog was set up by a Cabinet resolution, not by the Constitution or an Act.

q.s: The Development Monitoring and Evaluation Office (DMEO) is attached to:
q.x: DMEO is an attached office of NITI Aayog, the Government's think tank.

q.s: The nodal ministry for the PM POSHAN scheme is the Ministry of:
q.x: PM POSHAN (formerly Mid-Day Meal) is run by the Ministry of Education.

q.s: PM POSHAN covers children of Bal Vatika and classes:
q.x: PM POSHAN covers Bal Vatika and Classes I–VIII in government and aided schools.

q.s: India's first transgender college principal (2015) was:
q.x: Manabi Bandyopadhyay became principal of a college in West Bengal in 2015.

q.s: Joyita Mondal is known as India's first transgender:

q.s: Under the Factories Act, 1948, Inspectors are appointed by the:
q.x: The State Government appoints Inspectors; every District Magistrate is an Inspector for his district.

q.s: The minimum age for employment in a factory under the Factories Act, 1948 is:
q.x: No child below 14 may work in a factory under the Act.

q.x: e-Shram was launched on 26 August 2021 by the Ministry of Labour and Employment.

q.s: Workers registered on e-Shram receive a Universal Account Number of:
q.x: Registrants aged 16–59 get a 12-digit UAN; income-tax payers and EPFO/ESIC members are excluded.

q.x: ESI contributions are 3.25% by the employer and 0.75% by the employee; EPF is 12% each.

q.s: The Employees' Provident Fund scheme applies to establishments employing at least:
q.x: EPF covers establishments with 20 or more employees.

o: The Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs was formed by splitting the Ministry of Urban Development.
The Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs was formed in 2017 by merging two ministries.
PM SVANidhi loans are given only against collateral.
DAY-NULM is run by the Ministry of Rural Development.

q.s: PM SVANidhi gives collateral-free working-capital loans to:

q.s: The Andhra Pradesh school infrastructure scheme Mana Badi Nadu-Nedu has been renamed:

q.s: Jagananna Vasathi Deevena in Andhra Pradesh provided support for:
q.x: Vasathi Deevena met hostel and boarding costs; Vidya Deevena reimbursed fees.

q.s: The Rajiv Aarogyasri health scheme was started on 1 April 2007 under Chief Minister:
q.x: Aarogyasri began under Y.S. Rajasekhara Reddy; it is a State scheme run by the Dr NTR Vaidya Seva Trust.

q.s: In November 2014 the Aarogyasri scheme in Andhra Pradesh was renamed:
q.x: It was renamed NTR Vaidya Seva in November 2014.

q.s: As per Census 2011, persons with disabilities formed what share of India's population?
q.x: Census 2011 counted about 2.68 crore persons with disabilities, 2.21% of the population.

q.s: Which was the largest category of disability in Census 2011?
q.x: Movement disability was the largest category in Census 2011.

q.s: The Salma Dam (Afghan-India Friendship Dam), built with Indian help, is on which river?

q.s: Which Indian project in Afghanistan is NOT correctly matched?
o: Stor Palace – Restored with the Aga Khan Trust

q.s: India's maritime vision 'SAGAR' stands for:
o: Strategic Alliance for Growth and Regional Security
Security and Growth for All in the Region

q.s: The first woman to be Chief Economist of the IMF was:
q.x: Gita Gopinath took charge in January 2019; Raghuram Rajan (2003–06) was the youngest IMF chief economist.

q.s: The first President of the New Development Bank (BRICS Bank) was:
q.x: K.V. Kamath of India was the first NDB President (2015).

q.s: The Asian Development Bank is headquartered at:
q.x: The ADB is at Manila, Philippines; India is one of its 31 founding members.

q.s: Masato Kanda, who became the 11th President of the ADB in 2025, is from:
q.x: All ADB Presidents have been Japanese; Kanda took office in February 2025.

q.s: The theory of separation of powers was set out by Montesquieu in:
q.x: Montesquieu's The Spirit of Laws (1748) drew mainly on the British Constitution.

q.s: Dr. Ambedkar preferred the parliamentary system for India mainly because it:
o: Gives priority to stability over responsibility
Ensures a fixed term for the executive
Separates the executive from the legislature
Gives priority to responsibility over stability
q.x: Ambedkar said the parliamentary system offers more responsibility, though less stability, than the presidential.

q.s: The portfolio system in the Viceroy's Executive Council was introduced in 1859 by:
q.x: Canning began the portfolio system; Cornwallis first used the 1786 power to override the Council.

o: Government of India Act, 1919 – Lord Minto
First use of the 1786 override power – Lord Cornwallis
q.x: The 1919 Act came under Lord Chelmsford.

q.s: The Ninth Schedule was added to the Constitution by the:
q.x: The First Amendment added the Ninth Schedule with 13 Acts, protected by Article 31B.

q.s: In I.R. Coelho (2007), laws placed in the Ninth Schedule after which date were held open to judicial review?
q.x: 24 April 1973 is the date of the Kesavananda Bharati judgment.

q.s: The Supreme Court has held that the right to 'propagate' religion under Article 25 does not include the right to:
q.x: Propagation means spreading one's beliefs; converting another would impinge on that person's freedom of conscience.

q.s: Which Amendment provided that the enforcement of Articles 20 and 21 cannot be suspended during an emergency?
q.x: The 44th Amendment placed Articles 20 and 21 beyond an order under Article 359.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Preamble is correct?
o: It may be used to determine the ambit of Fundamental Rights.
It is justiciable in a court of law.
It is a source of power to the legislature.
It was enacted before the rest of the Constitution.
q.x: The Preamble is non-justiciable and no source of power, was enacted last, but helps interpret Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles.

q.s: The 42nd Amendment, 1976 was based on the recommendations of the:
q.x: The Swaran Singh Committee shaped the 42nd Amendment, passed during the Emergency.

q.s: The words 'Socialist' and 'Secular' were inserted in the Preamble between the words:
q.x: The 42nd Amendment made it 'Sovereign Socialist Secular Democratic Republic'.

q.s: Article 21A (Right to Education) was inserted in the Constitution by the:
q.x: The 86th Amendment inserted Article 21A; the RTE Act was passed in 2009.

q.s: Article 21A and the Right to Education Act came into force on:
q.x: Both came into force on 1 April 2010.

q.x: The Article 32 remedy is itself a Fundamental Right; Article 226 is discretionary and wider.

q.x: The 15th Amendment gave this extra-territorial writ power.

q.s: Which of the following can NOT be referred to a joint sitting of Parliament?

It causes delay and duplication in law-making.

An appeal lies to the Speaker against his rulings.
By law he must belong to the ruling party.

Merger of two-thirds of a party

q.x: Under Article 124(2) a judge retires at 65; there is no fixed tenure in years.

Availability below 1,700 cubic metres is called water-scarce.
Availability below 1,000 cubic metres is called water-stressed.

q.s: The Mulapeta (Bhavanapadu) greenfield port of Andhra Pradesh is in which district?

q.s: Under the Garbage Free City star rating, a 7-Star city must first be certified:

Jagananna Jeeva Kranthi – Sheep and goat units

o: Finance, real estate and professional services

q.s: In the Census, a 'marginal worker' is one who worked during the reference year for:
q.x: Main workers worked six months or more; marginal workers less than six months.

q.s: A person who works on another person's land for wages is classified in the Census as a/an:
q.x: A cultivator works own or leased land; an agricultural labourer works another's land for wages.

q.s: Which event of 1990–91 raised oil prices and cut remittances, pushing India into a balance-of-payments crisis?
q.x: The Gulf War raised the oil bill and cut Gulf remittances, draining reserves.

q.s: Lack of safe drinking water is an example of which kind of indicator of poverty?
q.x: Lack of safe water is a social indicator; monthly per capita consumption expenditure is an economic one.

q.x: The MPI covers health, education and living standards, not income.

q.s: In India, consumption inequality is measured mainly from:
o: The All India Debt and Investment Survey
q.x: MoSPI's HCES gives consumption data, though it may understate top incomes.

q.s: Wealth inequality in India is measured mainly from the:
o: All India Debt and Investment Survey

q.s: Which body was criticised as a 'super cabinet' and the 'fifth wheel of the coach'?
q.x: The Planning Commission was criticised for centralising decisions and eroding State autonomy.

q.s: The last (Twelfth) Five Year Plan prepared by the Planning Commission was approved by the:
q.x: The NDC approved the Twelfth Plan (2012–17); the Planning Commission was a non-statutory advisory body.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: NITI Aayog was set up by an executive resolution.
NITI Aayog was set up by an Act of Parliament in 2015.
The Planning Commission was a statutory body.
The Twelfth Plan was approved by NITI Aayog.
q.x: Both the Planning Commission and NITI Aayog are non-statutory; the NDC approved the Twelfth Plan.

q.s: In the 1991 New Economic Policy, short-term demand-management measures are known as:
q.x: Stabilisation (led by the IMF) was short-term demand management; structural adjustment (World Bank) was long-term and supply-side.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a stabilisation measure of the 1991 reforms?
q.x: Subsidy cuts, tight money and devaluation are stabilisation measures; trade liberalisation is structural adjustment.

q.s: The Sixteenth Finance Commission, whose grants include those for local bodies and disaster management, was chaired by:
q.x: Arvind Panagariya chaired the 16th FC; N.K. Singh chaired the 15th.

q.s: The City and Regional Growth Hubs (G-HUB) initiative, with Visakhapatnam as a pilot, is an initiative of:
o: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
q.x: G-HUB is NITI Aayog's initiative with four pilot city regions.

q.s: Notes and coins with no intrinsic value that are money only by government order are called:
q.x: Fiat money rests on government order; hard money is backed by gold or credible assets.

q.s: Which kind of money is NOT correctly matched with its meaning?
o: Fiat money – Money by government order
Near money – Time deposits and bills of exchange
Hard money – Backed by gold or credible assets
q.x: A token coin's face value is higher than the value of its metal.

q.s: According to the RBI's final count, about what share of the bank notes demonetised in 2016 came back?
q.x: The RBI Annual Report 2017–18 put the return at about 99.3%.

q.s: The liability of the government on the old ₹500 and ₹1,000 notes was ended by the:
o: Specified Bank Notes (Cessation of Liabilities) Act, 2017
q.x: The 2017 Act ended the liability on the specified bank notes.

q.s: The Andhra Pradesh microfinance crisis of 2010 was marked by:

Multiple lending, over-indebtedness and coercive recovery
A surplus of savings deposits with MFIs
A sharp fall in lending rates

q.s: Which of the following statements about the AP microfinance crisis of 2010 is correct?
o: After the crisis the MFI loan book expanded rapidly.
After the crisis the MFI loan book in Andhra Pradesh shrank sharply.
The crisis saw no borrower suicides.
It was caused by too little lending.
q.x: Multiple lending and coercive recovery led to the AP ordinance, after which MFI lending in AP collapsed.

q.s: Which was India's first credit rating agency, set up in 1987?
q.x: CRISIL dates from 1987, ICRA from 1991 and CARE from 1993.

q.s: Under the 15th Finance Commission, the net borrowing limit of States for 2021–22 was:
q.x: The limit was 4% in 2021–22, 3.5% in 2022–23 and 3% thereafter.

q.s: The additional borrowing allowed to States for power-sector reforms (2023–24 to 2025–26) was:
q.x: States could borrow an extra 0.5% of GSDP if they carried out power-sector reforms.

q.s: The Sixteenth Finance Commission recommended that the fiscal deficit of States be kept at:
q.x: It recommended 3% of GSDP for States and 3.5% of GDP for the Centre by 2030–31, with a wider deficit definition that includes off-budget borrowing.

q.s: Profession tax, levied by States with a ceiling of ₹2,500 per person a year, is provided for under Article:
q.x: Article 276 deals with profession tax; Article 271 lets the Union keep surcharges.

q.s: Which Constitutional Amendment made the net proceeds of all Union taxes shareable with the States from 1 April 1996?
q.x: The 80th Amendment (2000) followed the 10th FC's alternative scheme of devolution; cesses and surcharges remain outside.

q.s: Faceless assessment and the Taxpayers' Charter of the Income Tax Department were launched on:
q.x: The 'Transparent Taxation' platform with faceless assessment and the Charter was launched on 13 August 2020.

q.s: Project Insight of the Income Tax Department uses:
o: AI and data analytics for tax compliance
q.x: Project Insight analyses data to widen the tax base; e-Sahyog is an online check of mismatches.

q.s: In the Constitution, the Union Budget is referred to (Article 112) as the:
q.x: The word 'budget' is not used in the Constitution; Article 112 speaks of the Annual Financial Statement.

q.s: The Union Budget is the main instrument of:
q.x: The Budget performs allocation, redistribution and stabilisation as the tool of fiscal policy; monetary policy is the RBI's.

q.s: The theory of comparative advantage in international trade was propounded by:
q.x: Ricardo gave comparative advantage; Adam Smith gave absolute advantage.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: Export promotion is an outward-looking strategy.
Import substitution is an outward-looking strategy.
The 'direction' of trade is its commodity-wise pattern.
q.x: Export promotion looks outward and import substitution inward; direction is the country-wise pattern and composition the commodity-wise one.

q.s: The 14th WTO Ministerial Conference (March 2026) was held at:
q.x: MC14 was held at Yaounde, Cameroon; MC13 (2024) was at Abu Dhabi.

q.s: NAMA-11, a coalition of developing countries in the WTO, deals with:
q.x: NAMA-11 negotiates on market access for industrial goods.

q.s: The one-time amnesty for export-obligation defaults in the Foreign Trade Policy 2023 covers EPCG and:
q.x: The amnesty covers EPCG and Advance Authorisation; FTP 2023 also has Districts as Export Hubs and promotes rupee trade.

q.s: The EPCG scheme of the Foreign Trade Policy allows:
o: Duty-free import of inputs for export production
Rebate of taxes on apparel exports
Zero-duty import of capital goods against an export obligation
q.x: EPCG is for capital goods; Advance Authorisation covers inputs.

q.s: Which export scheme is NOT correctly matched with its purpose?
o: EPCG – Zero-duty capital goods against an export obligation
Advance Authorisation – Duty-free inputs for export production
RoSCTL – Rebate for apparel and made-ups
q.x: SEIS rewarded services exports.

q.s: During the 2013 'taper tantrum', Morgan Stanley placed India among the:
q.x: The Fragile Five were Brazil, India, Indonesia, South Africa and Turkey.

q.s: Which of the following capital inflows is regarded as self-sustaining?
q.x: FDI is the stable inflow; FCNR(B), ECB and FPI flows are temporary and can reverse.

q.s: As per the 11th Agriculture Census (2021–22), which district of Andhra Pradesh had the largest average operational holding?
q.x: Ananthapuram had the largest average holding and Visakhapatnam (0.40 ha) the smallest.

q.s: The buffer-stock norm for rice and wheat in the Central Pool is highest on which date?
q.x: The 1 July norm (411.2 lakh tonnes) is highest, after the rabi wheat harvest.

q.s: Which quarterly buffer-stock norm for rice and wheat is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: The 1 October norm is 307.7 lakh tonnes.

q.s: The genome-edited rice variety DRR Dhan 100 (Kamala) was developed from:
q.x: Kamala was edited from Samba Mahsuri.

q.s: Which kinds of genome editing carry no foreign DNA and fall outside India's GMO rules?
q.x: SDN-1 and SDN-2 edits have no foreign DNA; SDN-3 inserts foreign DNA.

q.s: ICAR's Lab to Land Programme was launched in:
q.x: Lab to Land began in 1979; the first KVK came in 1974.

q.s: The National Agricultural Technology Project (1998) was supported by the:
q.x: NATP was World Bank-aided; it was followed by NAIP (2006–14).

q.x: Exemptions for plantations, orchards and mechanised farms kept the redistribution below 2%.

q.s: Which of the following statements about land ceiling laws is correct?
o: They redistributed about a quarter of the cultivable area.
They exempted plantations, orchards and mechanised farms.
They applied uniformly with no exemptions.
They were enacted by the Union alone.
q.x: Wide exemptions kept redistribution below 2% of the cultivable area; land is a State subject.

q.s: Under Andhra Pradesh's Industrial Development Policy 4.0 (2024–29), a project is called 'Ultra-Mega' if its investment exceeds:

q.x: The policy targets a doubling of exports to US$40 billion.

q.x: Strikes and lockouts trouble large industries; the main SSI problem is lack of working capital.

q.s: The MSME Samadhaan portal (2017) addresses:
q.x: Samadhaan handles delayed-payment complaints; Udyam registration came in 2020.

q.s: The PM Vishwakarma scheme covers how many traditional trades?
q.x: PM Vishwakarma supports artisans in 18 trades; RAMP is a World Bank-backed MSME programme.

o: It reduces the government's equity in CPSEs.

It increases the government's equity in CPSEs.

q.s: Under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, which old-to-new pairing is NOT correct?
q.x: The AAIFR was replaced by the NCLAT.

q.s: The National Renewal Fund (1992) was meant to:

q.x: The NRF compensated and retrained workers; it was wound up in 2000.

q.s: The one-time restructuring of MSME loans without asset-classification downgrade (2019) was allowed by the:
q.x: The RBI permitted the 2019 restructuring.

q.s: The three economic regions of Andhra Pradesh are Visakhapatnam, Amaravati and:

Fourth, after Gujarat, Tamil Nadu and Maharashtra

q.x: Ramayapatnam is a non-captive (commercial) greenfield port in this cluster.

q.x: Tanneries were polluting the Palar in Tamil Nadu.

The SDGs were adopted at the Millennium Summit of 2000.
The SDGs are a voluntary agenda and not legally binding.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: Purchase of machinery is physical capital formation.
Purchase of machinery is human capital formation.
q.x: Machinery is physical capital; skills, education and health build human capital.

q.s: The largest moon of the solar system, bigger than the planet Mercury, is:

q.x: Titan has methane lakes about 100 m deep; Europa has a water ocean under its icy crust.

o: Reflection of light by the atmosphere
Atmospheric refraction of light from point sources
q.x: Air of changing density refracts starlight unevenly; planets show small discs and do not twinkle.

q.s: The rotation of the Earth was demonstrated by a pendulum experiment in Paris in 1851 by:
q.x: Foucault's pendulum proved the Earth's rotation; Aryabhata had explained day and night by rotation.

q.x: Winds are deflected to the right in the Northern and to the left in the Southern Hemisphere.

q.x: Laos is the only landlocked South-East Asian country.

q.x: Uzbekistan and Liechtenstein are the only doubly landlocked countries.

q.x: Westerlies blow from the south-west in the Northern and from the north-west in the Southern Hemisphere.

Subtropical high to the subpolar low
Equatorial low to the polar high
Polar high to the subpolar low

q.s: The Aravallis give little rain to Rajasthan because:

They lie in the rain shadow of the Western Ghats
The monsoon winds blow parallel to them
The winds reaching them are always offshore

q.s: The Tropic of Cancer passes through how many Indian States?
q.x: It crosses Gujarat, Rajasthan, MP, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura and Mizoram.

q.s: The Tropic of Cancer does NOT pass through which of the following States?
q.x: Odisha lies south of the Tropic of Cancer.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: Afghanistan is a part of the Indian subcontinent.
Bhutan lies to the north-west of India.
Afghanistan is not a member of SAARC.
Bhutan lies to the north-east of India.
q.x: Afghanistan, a SAARC member, is not part of the subcontinent; Bhutan lies to the north-east.

q.s: Through which pass does the Sutlej enter India?

q.s: Which Koeppen climate type is NOT correctly matched with its region in India?
q.x: 'As' (dry summer) is found on the Coromandel coast.

q.x: The Son is a right-bank tributary of the Ganga itself.

q.s: The Vamsadhara water dispute, whose award came in 2017, is between Andhra Pradesh and:

q.x: Drinking water comes first, then irrigation and power.

q.s: Under the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014, the Godavari River Management Board is located in:
q.x: The GRMB is in Telangana and the KRMB in Andhra Pradesh (Section 85).

q.s: Black (regur) soil corresponds in the USDA classification to:
q.x: Black soils are Vertisols with over 62% clay.

q.x: Black soil is rich in lime, iron, magnesia and potash but poor in nitrogen and phosphorus; its colour comes from titaniferous magnetite.

q.s: Among the pre-2022 districts of Andhra Pradesh, the largest notified forest area was in:
q.x: YSR Kadapa had the largest forest area and Krishna the lowest.

q.s: Among the pre-2022 districts of Andhra Pradesh, the lowest rainfall was received by:
